compare_blocks.body:
### Shared letters do not guarantee shared values

I describes attention and energy leaning toward the inner world, such as your own ideas and experience; F describes judgement that weighs values and the effect on people; P describes a preference for keeping plans and options open in the outside world. Two people may both care about honesty and still take different positions on disclosure, responsibility, cost or time together. Introversion does not mean a lack of social skill, a Feeling preference does not mean emotion replacing reasoning, and keeping options open does not mean being unable to commit.

### How Sensing and Intuition Use Information

The S description emphasises what actually happened and what can be observed or tried; the N description emphasises how pieces of information connect and how else they might be understood or used. Both kinds of information can serve the same task: an experience needs its meaning explained, and a possibility needs real conditions to test it.

S cannot be written as "only the immediate" with no grasp of abstraction, and N cannot be written as "detached from reality" or "deeper". A painting, a paragraph or a sport can involve experience, concept, technique and practice; interests and output formats cannot confirm S/N for you.

### ISFP and INFP: what Fi–Se and Fi–Ne actually claim

In type dynamics both types lead with an internal value judgement, Fi. ISFP's auxiliary Se describes engaging with concrete external information and direct experience; INFP's auxiliary Ne describes exploring external connections and possibilities. They help you ask "what matters here", "what did I actually notice" and "what else occurs to me", but they do not prove shared values, natural honesty or different mental abilities.

In the common four-function notation, ISFP lists a third process as Intuition with Te inferior, and INFP a third as Sensing with Te inferior. Sources differ on whether to label the third process introverted or extraverted: ISFP may be written Ni or Ne, INFP Si or Se, and this page uses the common version while keeping the disagreement visible. Te's theoretical position cannot establish that someone is bad at administration, numbers, leadership or execution, and it does not explain a particular criticism, impulse or mood change.

### Why one piece of work needs both experience and connection

Noticing that the text on an explainer card is too small is an observation about the concrete presentation; imagining that the illustration might make people think only certain participants are welcome is a hypothesis about meaning. You can start from either, but in both cases ask what real readers saw, which readings are only the author's inference, and whether the claim still holds when conditions change. S/N does not divide observation and interpretation into two exclusive jobs.

Two people may also want the same finished object while supporting it with different questions. Someone who tries a version first does not need to have mastered the craft, and someone who proposes a theme first is not thereby more creative. State the concrete difficulty, the intended expression, your personal boundary and the available conditions before deciding what to learn or revise; that carries more evidentiary weight than guessing an auxiliary function from the format of the work.

compare_blocks.body:
### The explainer card: attractive and meaningful — but can readers find how to join?

A fictional study group makes an explainer card for a community event. One person lays out a version first and watches whether the lettering, images and steps let participants know how to join; the other starts from the theme "anyone can take part" and explores different combinations of text and image. Both trying a version and exploring uses can help, and neither assigns one person the craft and the other the ideas.

Write the personal observation and the untested assumption in separate lines. A good sample does not mean the whole technique is mastered, and a meaningful theme does not guarantee the execution carries it. State what the card is meant to test, such as whether participants can find how to join after reading it, then fix the available materials, time, skills needed and people you can ask. If the sample looks good but readers misread the steps, the expression needs work; if the theme is meaningful but the practical information is missing, the concrete conditions need adding. Wanting the card yourself is not evidence that readers understood it.

Choose one change you can make and record what readers say before and after you try it. Ask willing readers to say what they understood and what they still do not know; one smooth trial read does not represent everyone's reading, and it cannot show which style suits a type. Decide whether to change the card or add explanation, and check whether that answers the original question. When comparing further study or work, you can look up the daily tasks and skill requirements of a role in the [FermatMind Career Library](/en/career), then check local training conditions, qualifications, cost and limits. This scene does not recommend buying a course or prove occupational fit; artist, writer and counsellor cannot be assigned by S/N.

### A shared activity: cherishing the story, and needing a quiet or seated option

(Fictional scene.) A friend proposes a shared activity because it connects to an experience you both value. You might think of that story first, or ask how it would actually run and whether you could take part comfortably. The story and the conditions can matter at the same time; one response does not prove a deeper grasp of feeling, and the other does not mean caring only about logistics.

Say separately what experience you hope for, what meaning you want to express, and what limits apply to time, cost, setting or the way you take part. Ask what the other person actually expects instead of inferring from type that "action is love" or that "only a long talk brings closeness". Where there is physical discomfort, deal with the practical condition and do not treat it as evidence of Se. If the event is loud or involves long standing, you can ask whether there is a quiet or seated way to take part; the other person does not owe a private reason to prove that a limit is legitimate. Wanting the occasion to be meaningful does not entitle anyone to demand conditions another person cannot bear.

You can change the format, scale the plan down, or arrange a different activity you both want. Explain the care and ask how to put it into practice, and explain why a particular action is not possible for now. Declining an activity is not rejecting the relationship, and accepting a proposal is not agreeing to every detail; negotiating boundaries and responsibilities is more useful than noting that you are both IFP.

### A draft: where exactly is "this part is unclear", and which use does it affect?

(Fictional scene.) A creative draft receives the comment "this part is unclear" and the deadline is close. Confirm three things first:

- Which passage did the reader see?
- What did they actually understand it to mean?
- What problem did they hope it would solve?

Ask for a specific location or example instead of deciding the reader does not understand your values, and do not throw out the whole piece because the comment was sharp.

Split the feedback into checkable fact, aesthetic or expressive preference, and your own emotional reaction. Acknowledging hurt does not require accepting every judgement, and holding to your intention does not remove the duty to explain. Check whether the issue is a factual error, an expression that did not land, different goals, or something not yet stated. Pick one part worth revising, keep the intention, then ask the reader to confirm whether the revision solved the problem. If the feedback is "I don't like this style", check first whether it conflicts with this particular need; you can keep the style and add the missing guidance. If you decline a specific change, give the reasoning and an alternative, without treating every criticism as an attack or promising to satisfy every preference.

State what can change this time, what cannot yet, and when you will return. If fatigue, prolonged discussion or workload is already clouding your judgement, adjust the load and seek support. Walking away, journalling, exercise or criticism cannot determine S/N, and cannot prove that a third function is "seized" or that recovery takes a fixed time; choose what helps you and watch the actual effect.

body: ISFP and INFP share Introversion, Feeling and Perceiving. They differ in how they prefer to take in information: ISFP has Sensing (S), which emphasizes concrete facts and direct experience, while INFP has Intuition (N), which emphasizes connections and possibilities. body: ### Shared letters do not guarantee shared values

I describes attention and energy leaning toward the inner world, such as your own ideas and experience; F describes judgement that weighs values and the effect on people; P describes a preference for keeping plans and options open in the outside world. Two people may both care about honesty and still take different positions on disclosure, responsibility, cost or time together. Introversion does not mean a lack of social skill, a Feeling preference does not mean emotion replacing reasoning, and keeping options open does not mean being unable to commit.
### How Sensing and Intuition Use Information

The S description emphasises what actually happened and what can be observed or tried; the N description emphasises how pieces of information connect and how else they might be understood or used. Both kinds of information can serve the same task: an experience needs its meaning explained, and a possibility needs real conditions to test it.

S cannot be written as "only the immediate" with no grasp of abstraction, and N cannot be written as "detached from reality" or "deeper". A painting, a paragraph or a sport can involve experience, concept, technique and practice; interests and output formats cannot confirm S/N for you.

In type dynamics both types lead with an internal value judgement, Fi. ISFP's auxiliary Se describes engaging with concrete external information and direct experience; INFP's auxiliary Ne describes exploring external connections and possibilities. Te's theoretical position cannot establish that someone is bad at administration, numbers, leadership or execution, and it does not explain a particular criticism, impulse or mood change.

Noticing that the text on an explainer card is too small is an observation about the concrete presentation; imagining that the illustration might make people think only certain participants are welcome is a hypothesis about meaning. You can start from either, but in both cases ask what real readers saw, which readings are only the author's inference, and whether the claim still holds when conditions change. S/N does not divide observation and interpretation into two exclusive jobs.

Two people may also want the same finished object while supporting it with different questions. Someone who tries a version first does not need to have mastered the craft, and someone who proposes a theme first is not thereby more creative. State the concrete difficulty, the intended expression, your personal boundary and the available conditions before deciding what to learn or revise; that carries more evidentiary weight than guessing an auxiliary function from the format of the work.

body: ### The explainer card: attractive and meaningful — but can readers find how to join?

A fictional study group makes an explainer card for a community event. One person lays out a version first and watches whether the lettering, images and steps let participants know how to join; the other starts from the theme "anyone can take part" and explores different combinations of text and image. Both trying a version and exploring uses can help, and neither assigns one person the craft and the other the ideas.

Write the personal observation and the untested assumption in separate lines. A good sample does not mean the whole technique is mastered, and a meaningful theme does not guarantee the execution carries it. State what the card is meant to test, such as whether participants can find how to join after reading it, then fix the available materials, time, skills needed and people you can ask. Wanting the card yourself is not evidence that readers understood it.

Choose one change you can make and record what readers say before and after you try it. Ask willing readers to say what they understood and what they still do not know; one smooth trial read does not represent everyone's reading, and it cannot show which style suits a type. (Fictional scene.) A friend proposes a shared activity because it connects to an experience you both value. You might think of that story first, or ask how it would actually run and whether you could take part comfortably. You can change the format, scale the plan down, or arrange a different activity you both want. (Fictional scene.) A creative draft receives the comment "this part is unclear" and the deadline is close. Confirm three things first:

- Which passage did the reader see?
- What did they actually understand it to mean?
- What problem did they hope it would solve?

If you decline a specific change, give the reasoning and an alternative, without treating every criticism as an attack or promising to satisfy every preference.

State what can change this time, what cannot yet, and when you will return. If fatigue, prolonged discussion or workload is already clouding your judgement, adjust the load and seek support. Walking away, journalling, exercise or criticism cannot determine S/N, and cannot prove that a third function is "seized" or that recovery takes a fixed time; choose what helps you and watch the actual effect.

**Craft and words.** Writing, painting, music and hands-on interests cannot prove an auxiliary process, and cannot predict talent or occupational competence.

body: The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; sharing letters does not make different instruments equivalent. Type descriptions and cognitive functions are theoretical readings, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not describe a nationally representative sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types, and found overlap with several dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument versions and samples cannot be mixed: the publisher describes later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of FermatMind scores. That specific study cannot validate the scenarios here, determine an individual's type, or settle every question raised by later instruments.

Erford et al. (2025) separately reviewed 193 studies published between 1999 and 2024 that used the English MBTI Form M, reporting good internal consistency (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence with similar constructs. They excluded studies already reported in the test manuals to keep the samples independent. None of the included studies reported evidence on structural validity or test–retest reliability. Consistency of scores does not confirm natural types, and it does not validate A/T or transfer to the FermatMind assessment. Supporting evidence and research gaps both have to be read against a specific instrument and sample.

The scenarios and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or population findings. Use them against your own experience and counterexamples; a type alone cannot diagnose, hire, select a career or screen a partner.

A fictional study group makes an explainer card for a community event. (Fictional scene.) A friend proposes a shared activity because it connects to an experience you both value. - What did they actually understand it to mean?
- What problem did they hope it would solve?

Split the feedback into checkable fact, aesthetic or expressive preference, and your own emotional reaction. Acknowledging hurt does not require accepting every judgement, and holding to your intention does not remove the duty to explain. Check whether the issue is a factual error, an expression that did not land, different goals, or something not yet stated. compare_blocks.body:
### Six common misreads of ISFP and INFP

**Craft and words.** Writing, painting, music and hands-on interests cannot prove an auxiliary process, and cannot predict talent or occupational competence.

**Experience and depth.** Concrete information can be very complex, and abstract explanation can be shallow; S/N does not rank depth of thought.

**Sincerity and shared values.** Sharing Fi is a theoretical description; it does not prove identical principles on a particular question, an ability to see through pretence, or that someone will never hurt another person.

**Execution and administration.** A shared inferior Te does not prove that both are bad at planning or managing costs; skills, experience, tools and task conditions have to be established in practice.

**Stress behaviour and maturity.** Walking, journalling, withdrawing or snapping all have many causes; they cannot type someone on their own, and cannot be used to rate maturity, health or recovery speed.

**Relationships and the suffix.** Shared letters do not guarantee compatibility; A/T cannot resolve S/N either, and cannot decide who would be the better partner.

faq_blocks.answer:
The four-letter difference is S/N: taking information more from concrete facts and experience, or attending more to connections and possibilities. Both need facts and interpretation to finish a real task; this is not the line between artists and writers, and it does not score depth or execution.

In the fictional card example, give both people the same text and reader feedback. One useful question is, “Where exactly did the reader get stuck?” Another is, “Could the same wording lead readers to misunderstand other parts of the card?” Both questions can improve the same piece of work. The order in which someone asks them cannot establish a type.
faq_blocks.question: What is the main difference between ISFP and INFP?

faq_blocks.answer:
No. Shared I/F/P, or Fi in theory, does not imply the same personal principles, relationship expectations, cost arrangements or willingness to take responsibility. Two people may both value honesty and still set different boundaries about telling a story publicly.

State separately what you care about and what you are willing to share or carry, then listen to the person's own answer; do not read the absence of an explicit refusal as agreement. Shared letters describe preferences in sourcing and judging, not your positions on a specific question.
faq_blocks.question: Do shared I, F and P mean the same values?

faq_blocks.answer:
No. This page uses the theoretical vocabulary of type dynamics: Fi describes internal value judgement, Se describes concrete external experience, Ne describes external connections and possibilities. They cannot measure natural honesty, craft, writing ability or the cause of stress.

Direct experience and conceptual thinking are both available to one person, and any interpretation still has to be checked against facts and counterexamples. When you meet a function abbreviation, confirm which four-position convention the author uses, then whether it is meant to describe taking in information or making a decision.
faq_blocks.question: Are Fi–Se and Fi–Ne measured psychological mechanisms?

faq_blocks.answer:
The common four-function notation selects Ni for ISFP and Si for INFP, but the third process is identified by its function, and sources differ on whether to label it introverted or extraverted: ISFP may be Ni or Ne, INFP Si or Se.

Because the direction is interpreted differently, it cannot be written as a single psychological mechanism, and function maturity certainly cannot be judged from midlife or childhood experience. A shared inferior Te also does not prove that both are bad at administration, budgeting or organising.
faq_blocks.question: Are the third functions always Ni and Si?

faq_blocks.answer:
No. Output format, hobbies and technique are not preference measures; training, experience, task conditions and opportunity all affect performance. Writers also need concrete material, craft also needs conceptual judgement, and numerical ability has to be seen in real task performance.

Even if you enjoy both kinds of activity, you can leave the question open instead of choosing S/N by ability or interest. To tell the two apart, return to which kind of information each notices first in the same task.
faq_blocks.question: Can writing, hands-on work or handling numbers determine the type?

faq_blocks.answer:
Ask for the specific location, the reader's understanding and the goal of the piece, and separate factual error, unclear expression, style preference and your own hurt. Deal first with the part that affects the goal, say whether you are keeping the intention or changing the form, then check whether the reader's original problem is solved.

You can decline a particular change, but give the reason; feedback is not the same as a verdict on your personality. Both types may revise the expression first or the goal first, and that difference is not a basis for typing.
faq_blocks.question: How do you continue when a draft is criticised?

faq_blocks.answer:

Understand the real burden and available support, choose a workable option and watch the effect; do not type anyone from an action or a recovery time. If you also have an A/T result, it is one clue about self-assessment and pressure response, unrelated to S/N.

body: ### Shared letters do not guarantee shared values

I describes attention and energy leaning toward the inner world, such as your own ideas and experience; F describes judgement that weighs values and the effect on people; P describes a preference for keeping plans and options open in the outside world. Two people may both care about honesty and still take different positions on disclosure, responsibility, cost or time together. Introversion does not mean a lack of social skill, a Feeling preference does not mean emotion replacing reasoning, and keeping options open does not mean being unable to commit.
### How Sensing and Intuition Use Information

The S description emphasises what actually happened and what can be observed or tried; the N description emphasises how pieces of information connect and how else they might be understood or used. Both kinds of information can serve the same task: an experience needs its meaning explained, and a possibility needs real conditions to test it.

S cannot be written as "only the immediate" with no grasp of abstraction, and N cannot be written as "detached from reality" or "deeper". A painting, a paragraph or a sport can involve experience, concept, technique and practice; interests and output formats cannot confirm S/N for you.

In type dynamics both types lead with an internal value judgement, Fi. ISFP's auxiliary Se describes engaging with concrete external information and direct experience; INFP's auxiliary Ne describes exploring external connections and possibilities. sections.body_md:
### Shared letters do not guarantee shared values

I describes attention and energy leaning toward the inner world, such as your own ideas and experience; F describes judgement that weighs values and the effect on people; P describes a preference for keeping plans and options open in the outside world. Two people may both care about honesty and still take different positions on disclosure, responsibility, cost or time together. Introversion does not mean a lack of social skill, a Feeling preference does not mean emotion replacing reasoning, and keeping options open does not mean being unable to commit.

### How Sensing and Intuition Use Information

The S description emphasises what actually happened and what can be observed or tried; the N description emphasises how pieces of information connect and how else they might be understood or used. Both kinds of information can serve the same task: an experience needs its meaning explained, and a possibility needs real conditions to test it.

S cannot be written as "only the immediate" with no grasp of abstraction, and N cannot be written as "detached from reality" or "deeper". A painting, a paragraph or a sport can involve experience, concept, technique and practice; interests and output formats cannot confirm S/N for you.

### ISFP and INFP: what Fi–Se and Fi–Ne actually claim

In type dynamics both types lead with an internal value judgement, Fi. ISFP's auxiliary Se describes engaging with concrete external information and direct experience; INFP's auxiliary Ne describes exploring external connections and possibilities. They help you ask "what matters here", "what did I actually notice" and "what else occurs to me", but they do not prove shared values, natural honesty or different mental abilities.

In the common four-function notation, ISFP lists a third process as Intuition with Te inferior, and INFP a third as Sensing with Te inferior. Sources differ on whether to label the third process introverted or extraverted: ISFP may be written Ni or Ne, INFP Si or Se, and this page uses the common version while keeping the disagreement visible. Te's theoretical position cannot establish that someone is bad at administration, numbers, leadership or execution, and it does not explain a particular criticism, impulse or mood change.

### Why one piece of work needs both experience and connection

Noticing that the text on an explainer card is too small is an observation about the concrete presentation; imagining that the illustration might make people think only certain participants are welcome is a hypothesis about meaning. You can start from either, but in both cases ask what real readers saw, which readings are only the author's inference, and whether the claim still holds when conditions change. S/N does not divide observation and interpretation into two exclusive jobs.

Two people may also want the same finished object while supporting it with different questions. Someone who tries a version first does not need to have mastered the craft, and someone who proposes a theme first is not thereby more creative. State the concrete difficulty, the intended expression, your personal boundary and the available conditions before deciding what to learn or revise; that carries more evidentiary weight than guessing an auxiliary function from the format of the work.
